sources.entry: Maintainerr | Rule-based cleanup of unwatched media in Plex and Jellyfin

summary.one_liner: Maintainerr is a self-hosted, rule-based tool that finds unwatched or unrequested media in Plex, Jellyfin or Emby and cleans it up through a grace-period collection and configurable deletion actions.
summary.what_it_does: Users write rules (combined with AND/OR logic) using properties from Plex, Jellyfin, Emby, Radarr, Sonarr, Sportarr, Seerr, Ombi, Tautulli, Streamystats and Tracearr. Matching items are gathered into a collection and held for a configurable grace period before action. Actions include deleting files from disk, unmonitoring or deleting in Radarr/Sonarr/Sportarr, changing quality profile, clearing requests in Seerr or Ombi, and deleting from the download client. It can also render overlays onto posters, send notifications through several services, and import or export rules as YAML. Runs can be scheduled with cron, and the README lists an OpenAPI/Swagger API and health endpoints.
use_cases: automatically delete unwatched movies and TV shows
free up disk space on a Plex or Jellyfin server
clean up media that was requested but never watched
set a grace period before removing old media
manage a 'leaving soon' collection on Plex
how_to_run: docker run -d --name maintainerr -e TZ=Europe/Brussels -v ./data:/opt/data -u 1000:1000 -p 6246:6246 --restart unless-stopped ghcr.io/maintainerr/maintainerr:latest
Alternatively, use the Docker Compose, Podman Quadlet or Kubernetes examples in the README
Ensure the /opt/data volume is readable and writable by UID:GID 1000:1000 (or the configured user)
stack: sharp (image processing, requires x86-64-v2 on x86 CPUs)
notable: Rules span many sources (media servers, *arr apps, request managers, Tautulli, Streamystats, Tracearr) with AND/OR logic
Collections can be kept inside Maintainerr without creating one on the media server
Grace-period collection before any deletion action, optionally shown as a 'Leaving soon' Plex shelf
Community rule library and YAML import/export with cross-server migration
Weekly anonymous telemetry, which can be disabled with TELEMETRY=off
caveats: Image overlays and collection posters need an x86-64-v2 CPU on x86 (disabled otherwise; not required on arm64)
Deletion actions are destructive, so rules and grace periods need careful configuration
Some integrations are limited to specific servers (Tautulli is Plex-only, Streamystats is Jellyfin-only)
